read_gate_ablations.conclusion: the regression is per-object memory traffic for the transform (64 B matrix) and appearance rows, not the call shape, the validation or the Result wrapper. Removing the reads entirely returns the arm to the pre-PD level (0.8247), but no available restructuring recovers it.
read_gate_ablations.next_step: data-layout experiment: measure bytes touched per object in both arms and decide whether the presentation read may carry a compact pre-gathered row. That touches the read contract, so it is an owner-scoped change, not a local fix.

gpu_time_of_that_draw.note: timer query around the GPU command range; effectively zero

window_visibility_control.conclusion: not a hidden-window or compositor-visibility effect

pause_cause.conclusion: the 175-190 ms stall is the process's SECOND SwapWindow, independent of the frozen flag. In the registered workload the second present is the first paused frame, so the overrun lands inside the first pause; with one warm live frame the stall moves there and the first pause costs 0.7 ms.
pause_cause.implication: the gate reading is honest for the registered workload, but the cause is a one-time swap chain stall rather than the pause path. A product-representative pause (swap chain already warm) measures 0.4-0.9 ms in the same runs.
fix_options: present one warm frame after the first frame at startup, so the stall is paid inside load (2000 ms budget, currently 410 ms) and not inside the first pause; the first_frame_presented boundary is unchanged because the extra present happens after it
register a controls workload that presents N live frames before the first control, and report both readings
